# Tool reference

<!-- GENERATED by `pnpm docs:tools` from the tool definitions. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every tool the CXCaller MCP server exposes (52 in all), with its parameters exactly as an agent sees them. For how to use them together, see the [usage guide](./usage-guide.md).

Conventions: arguments are `snake_case`; ids are UUIDs; phone numbers are E.164 (`+94771234567`). **Required** parameters are marked; everything else is optional. A parameter typed `… \| null` accepts `null` to clear a value, whereas leaving it out leaves the value unchanged.

Tags: `read-only` never changes anything · `changes data` writes · `can place calls` may cause a real phone to ring · `destructive` deletes or cannot be undone.

## Account and reference

### `get_account`

`read-only`

Shows which CXCaller organization this API key is bound to (id, name, default timezone) and the key's own name. Every other tool already targets this organization automatically; call this to confirm you are connected to the right account.

_No parameters._

### `list_caller_ids`

`read-only`

Lists the phone numbers calls can come from: the shared pool (available to every account; use caller_id.source "shared_pool" and the dialer picks one per call) and the organization's own claimed dedicated numbers (pin one with source "dedicated" and its id). Numbers cannot be claimed or released with an API key.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | integer (min 1, max 9007199254740991) |  | 1-based page number. Default 1. |
| `take` | integer (min 1, max 50) |  | Items per page, 1–50. Default 10. |
| `include` | `"both"` \| `"dedicated"` \| `"pool"` |  | Which list to return. Default "both". |

### `list_available_numbers`

`read-only`

Dedicated numbers no organization holds yet, which an owner or admin can claim in the CXCaller dashboard to call from exclusively. They cannot be claimed with an API key. Calls can always use the shared pool without claiming anything.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | integer (min 1, max 9007199254740991) |  | 1-based page number. Default 1. |
| `take` | integer (min 1, max 50) |  | Items per page, 1–50. Default 10. |

### `get_phone_number`

`read-only`

One phone number by id: a shared-pool number or one this organization has claimed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `phone_number_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

## Campaigns

### `list_voices`

`read-only`

Lists the voices an agent can speak with (pass one as voice_id). Exactly one is the default.

_No parameters._

### `list_campaigns`

`read-only`

Lists campaigns with their status and headline stats. Filter by lifecycle status or search by name.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | integer (min 1, max 9007199254740991) |  | 1-based page number. Default 1. |
| `take` | integer (min 1, max 50) |  | Items per page, 1–50. Default 10. |
| `query` | string |  | Search by name. |
| `status` | `"draft"` \| `"scheduled"` \| `"running"` \| `"paused"` \| `"completed"` \| `"cancelled"` \| `"failed"` |  |  |

### `get_campaign`

`read-only`

Full configuration of one campaign (agent, schedule, caller ID, status, stats) plus its declared outcome fields. Status is one of draft, scheduled, running, paused, completed, cancelled, failed. reviewStatus is the content verification a launch needs: unverified, pending, approved, flagged (held for a CXCaller admin) or rejected, with reviewReason.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaign_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Campaign id. |

### `create_campaign`

`changes data` `can place calls`

Creates a calling campaign in one step: the agent (instructions, language, voice), schedule and pacing, caller ID, the structured data to extract (outcome_fields), and who to call. By default it is created as a DRAFT and nothing is dialed; review it, then run launch_campaign. Pass launch=true to dispatch immediately. Launching first needs the platform's content review to approve the instructions; run verify_campaign on the draft to learn the verdict before asking the user to confirm. A launched campaign starts calling within about 20 seconds, so only launch when the user has asked you to place these calls. Recipients come from `recipients` (phone numbers; contacts are created if new), `group_ids` and/or `contact_ids`. Defaults: each recipient is called once (max_attempts 1) and only one call is in flight at a time (max_concurrent_calls 1), so raise max_concurrent_calls for anything larger than a handful of people.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `instructions` | string \| null |  | The voice agent's system prompt: who it is, who it is calling, what to say, what to find out, when to end the call. Reference per-recipient values as {{variable_name}}; every recipient must then have that variable or the call fails before dialing. Values without a placeholder are still shown to the agent as context. null clears it. |
| `objective` | string \| null |  | One sentence on what a successful call achieves. Steers the post-call summary and extraction, not the live conversation. |
| `language` | string \| null |  | Language the agent speaks: BCP-47 tag or name ("si", "si-LK" and "Sinhala" all work). |
| `voice_id` | string \| null |  | A voice from list_voices (case-sensitive). null restores the default voice. |
| `shared_variables` | object |  | Variables given to every recipient, e.g. {"company":"IIT"}. A recipient's own variables override these. |
| `transfer_to` | string |  | E.164 number the agent may warm-transfer the caller to. |
| `scheduled_start_at` | string (date-time) \| null |  | ISO 8601 start time. null/omitted = start as soon as launched. |
| `calling_window_start` | string \| null |  | Earliest local time of day to dial, "HH:MM". null = no lower bound. |
| `calling_window_end` | string \| null |  | Latest local time of day to dial, "HH:MM". An end before the start spans midnight. null = no upper bound. |
| `calling_days` | array of integer (min 1, max 7) |  | ISO weekdays to dial on, 1 = Monday … 7 = Sunday. Empty array = every day. |
| `respect_contact_timezone` | boolean |  | Use each contact's own timezone for the calling window when they have one. |
| `timezone` | string |  | IANA timezone for the calling window, e.g. "Asia/Colombo". |
| `max_attempts` | integer (min 1, max 10) |  | Total calls per recipient including the first. Platform default 1. |
| `retry_delay_minutes` | integer (min 0, max 9007199254740991) |  |  |
| `retry_on_dispositions` | array of `"no_answer"` \| `"busy"` \| `"failed"` \| `"declined"` \| `"voicemail"` \| `"completed"` |  | Outcomes that trigger another attempt. Default: no_answer, busy, failed. |
| `max_concurrent_calls` | integer (min 1, max 9007199254740991) |  | Simultaneous calls for this campaign. Platform default 1, meaning one person is called at a time. |
| `caller_id` | object {source, phone_number_id} |  | Which number the calls come from. |
| `caller_id.source` | `"shared_pool"` \| `"dedicated"` | yes | "shared_pool": the dialer picks the least busy pool number per call (default, included with any plan). "dedicated": pin one number this organization has claimed. |
| `caller_id.phone_number_id` | string (uuid) |  | Required for "dedicated", forbidden for "shared_pool". Get ids from list_caller_ids. |
| `outcome_fields` | array of object {key, label, type, options, is_kpi} |  | What to extract from each conversation. Declare these BEFORE calls run: without them results only contain a free-text summary, no structured answers. A field the caller never answered comes back null. |
| `outcome_fields[].key` | string | yes | Machine key, e.g. "paid" or "callback_date". |
| `outcome_fields[].label` | string | yes | Human label, e.g. "Paid?". |
| `outcome_fields[].type` | `"text"` \| `"number"` \| `"boolean"` \| `"enum"` \| `"json"` | yes |  |
| `outcome_fields[].options` | array of string |  | Allowed values; only for type "enum". |
| `outcome_fields[].is_kpi` | boolean |  | Highlight as a headline KPI on the campaign overview. |
| `recipients` | array of object {phone, name, language, variables} |  |  |
| `recipients[].phone` | string | yes |  |
| `recipients[].name` | string |  | How the agent addresses them; available to the prompt as {{contact_name}}. |
| `recipients[].language` | string |  |  |
| `recipients[].variables` | object |  | Per-recipient values, e.g. {"payment_amount":"20000"}. Highest precedence. |
| `group_ids` | array of string (uuid) |  |  |
| `contact_ids` | array of string (uuid) |  |  |
| `launch` | boolean |  | Dispatch immediately after creating. Default false (leave as a draft for review). |

### `update_campaign`

`changes data`

Edits a campaign. Only draft or scheduled campaigns are editable; a running, paused or finished one is rejected (cancel then reactivate to edit). Send only what should change; omitted fields are untouched and null clears a nullable field. caller_id and outcome_fields replace their current values. Actually changing instructions or objective voids the content verification (reviewStatus back to unverified) and takes a SCHEDULED campaign back to draft, so it must be launched again.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaign_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Campaign id. |
| `name` | string |  |  |

Reference per-recipient values as {{variable_name}}; every recipient must then have that variable or the call fails before dialing. Values without a placeholder are still shown to the agent as context. null clears it. |

### `duplicate_campaign`

`changes data`

Copies any campaign (even a finished one) into a new DRAFT with the same agent, schedule, pacing and caller ID. Nothing is dialed. Recipients are copied fresh (queued, no attempts) unless include_recipients is false. The start time is not copied: the copy starts when launched. The copy needs its own content review before launch (verify_campaign / launch_campaign). Use it to call the same people again after a campaign finished.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaign_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Campaign id. |
| `name` | string |  | Default: the source name with " (copy)". |
| `include_recipients` | boolean |  | Default true. |

### `add_campaign_recipients`

`changes data`

Adds people to a draft or scheduled campaign, from `recipients` (phone numbers; contacts are created if new), contact groups, and/or existing contacts. Suppressed contacts are skipped and duplicates ignored. A group is copied in at this moment; later changes to the group do not flow in.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaign_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Campaign id. |
| `recipients` | array of object {phone, name, language, variables} |  |  |
| `recipients[].phone` | string | yes |  |
| `recipients[].name` | string |  | How the agent addresses them; available to the prompt as {{contact_name}}. |
| `recipients[].language` | string |  |  |
| `recipients[].variables` | object |  | Per-recipient values, e.g. {"payment_amount":"20000"}. Highest precedence. |
| `group_ids` | array of string (uuid) |  |  |
| `contact_ids` | array of string (uuid) |  |  |

`read-only`

Lists who is on a campaign and how far each got. `group` buckets statuses: pending (queued/scheduled), active (dialing/in_progress), done (completed), needs_attention (no_answer/failed/exhausted), skipped (suppressed/cancelled).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaign_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Campaign id. |
| `page` | integer (min 1, max 9007199254740991) |  | 1-based page number. Default 1. |
| `take` | integer (min 1, max 50) |  | Items per page, 1–50. Default 10. |
| `query` | string |  | Search by name or phone. |
| `group` | `"pending"` \| `"active"` \| `"done"` \| `"needs_attention"` \| `"skipped"` |  |  |
| `status` | `"queued"` \| `"scheduled"` \| `"dialing"` \| `"in_progress"` \| `"completed"` \| `"no_answer"` \| `"failed"` \| `"exhausted"` \| `"suppressed"` \| `"cancelled"` |  | Exact status; overrides group. |

`read-only`

One person on a campaign in full: status, variables, prompt override, and every call made to them. Use the recipient id from list_campaign_recipients.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaign_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Campaign id. |
| `recipient_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

### `update_campaign_recipients`

`changes data`

Edits what the agent knows about specific people on a campaign. `variables` are merged into each recipient's existing ones (keys not sent are kept). `context_override` replaces the whole system prompt for that one person (null removes it). Changing a context_override is reviewed content: it needs a draft or scheduled campaign, voids the content verification, and takes a scheduled campaign back to draft, so it must be verified and launched again. Variables alone can be changed at any time.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaign_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Campaign id. |
| `updates` | array of object {recipient_id, variables, context_override} | yes |  |
| `updates[].recipient_id` | string (uuid) | yes | From list_campaign_recipients. |
| `updates[].variables` | object |  |  |
| `updates[].context_override` | string \| null |  |  |

### `remove_campaign_recipients`

`changes data` `destructive`

Takes people off a campaign before they are called. Only recipients still queued or scheduled are removed; anyone already dialed is silently left in place, so check list_campaign_recipients afterwards. The contacts themselves are kept.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaign_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Campaign id. |
| `recipient_ids` | array of string (uuid) | yes | From list_campaign_recipients. |

### `retry_campaign_recipient`

`changes data` `can place calls`

Puts a recipient whose status is no_answer, failed or exhausted back in the queue for another attempt (any other status is rejected). It only gets dialed while the campaign is RUNNING: on a paused campaign it waits for resume, and a completed, cancelled or failed campaign is never dialed again, so this refuses there. To call people from a finished campaign again, create a new campaign for them. Use the recipient id from list_campaign_recipients.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaign_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Campaign id. |
| `recipient_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

### `launch_campaign`

`changes data` `can place calls`

DISPATCHES a draft campaign: it will start placing real phone calls to every recipient within about 20 seconds (or at its scheduled start). Only call this when the user has asked you to start these calls. The campaign must be complete (recipients, caller ID, and instructions); if not, the error lists what is missing. Its content must also pass the platform's review: this submits it if needed and waits up to 80 s for the verdict. If the review flags or rejects it, or has not answered in time, nothing is dialed and the error says what to do. Use control_campaign to pause or cancel afterwards.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaign_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Campaign id. |

### `verify_campaign`

`changes data`

Submits a draft or scheduled campaign's content (instructions, objective, per-recipient prompt overrides) to the platform's review, which must approve it before the campaign can launch, and waits up to 80 s for the verdict. Nothing is dialed. launch_campaign does this itself; call this first to tell the user the verdict before they confirm a launch. reviewStatus: approved (can launch), pending (still being reviewed; call again), flagged (held for a CXCaller admin; cannot launch until approved), rejected (change the content, then verify again).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaign_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Campaign id. |

### `control_campaign`

`changes data` `can place calls`

Moves a campaign through its lifecycle. pause: stop dialing new calls (calls already in progress finish). resume: continue a paused campaign. cancel: stop for good, though a cancelled campaign can be reactivated. reactivate: turn a cancelled campaign back into an editable draft.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaign_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Campaign id. |
| `action` | `"pause"` \| `"resume"` \| `"cancel"` \| `"reactivate"` | yes |  |

### `delete_campaign`

`changes data` `destructive`

Deletes a draft, cancelled, completed or failed campaign: it disappears from lists, while its call history is kept. A scheduled, running or paused campaign must be cancelled first (control_campaign).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaign_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Campaign id. |

### `delete_campaigns`

`changes data` `destructive`

Deletes up to 100 campaigns at once, like delete_campaign. Scheduled, running or paused ones are skipped rather than failing the batch: `skipped` lists each with its reason (not_deletable: cancel it first; not_found).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaign_ids` | array of string (uuid) | yes |  |

### `get_campaign_stats`

`read-only`

Live progress of a campaign: recipients (queued/completed/failed), calls made, connect rate, minutes, cost, and a breakdown of how calls ended. Refreshes every ~5 s while running; poll no faster than every 5 s, and stop once status is completed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaign_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Campaign id. |

### `get_live_calls`

`read-only`

Who a campaign is on the phone with right now: the calls currently dialing or in progress. Empty when nothing is in flight.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaign_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Campaign id. |

### `get_campaign_outcomes`

`read-only`

What the calls found out: per-field tallies for the outcome_fields declared on the campaign (yes/no counts, numeric summaries, top values). Set include_recipients for the per-person answers, and field_key (+ value) to list who gave a particular answer. Counts are per recipient (their latest answer), not per call.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaign_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Campaign id. |
| `include_recipients` | boolean |  | Also return per-recipient answers. |
| `field_key` | string |  | With include_recipients: only recipients who answered this field. |
| `value` | string |  | With field_key: only recipients whose answer equals this (case-insensitive). |
| `page` | integer (min 1, max 9007199254740991) |  | 1-based page number. Default 1. |
| `take` | integer (min 1, max 50) |  | Items per page, 1–50. Default 10. |

## Calls

### `make_call`

`changes data` `can place calls`

PLACES A REAL PHONE CALL to one person, made by an AI voice agent following your `instructions`. Only call this when the user has asked you to call this number, and never to numbers they did not give you. Before dialing, the platform's content review must approve the instructions; this waits for it (usually under a minute). If it flags or rejects them, nothing is dialed and the error says why. Dialing then starts within about 20 seconds (the platform dispatches on a 20 s cycle) and the call is made once unless max_attempts says otherwise. Internally this creates and launches a one-recipient campaign, so the call also appears in the dashboard. It returns immediately with a campaign_id; poll get_call_result until finished is true (a call takes roughly 30 s to a few minutes), or set wait_seconds to wait here for up to 80 s. To collect structured answers (e.g. "did they agree to a callback?") declare outcome_fields; otherwise you only get a transcript and free-text summary.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `to` | string | yes | Number to call, E.164. |
| `name` | string |  | The person's name; the agent can use it as {{contact_name}}. |
| `instructions` | string | yes | The voice agent's system prompt: who it is, who it is calling, what to say, what to find out, and when to end the call. Reference values from `variables` as {{name}}. |
| `variables` | object |  | Facts about this person for the agent, e.g. {"payment_amount":"20000","due_date":"21 May"}. |
| `objective` | string \| null |  | One sentence on what a successful call achieves. Steers the post-call summary and extraction, not the live conversation. |
| `language` | string \| null |  | Language the agent speaks: BCP-47 tag or name ("si", "si-LK" and "Sinhala" all work). |
| `voice_id` | string \| null |  | A voice from list_voices (case-sensitive). null restores the default voice. |
| `transfer_to` | string |  | E.164 number the agent may warm-transfer the caller to. |
| `caller_id` | object {source, phone_number_id} |  | Defaults to the shared pool. |
| `caller_id.source` | `"shared_pool"` \| `"dedicated"` | yes | "shared_pool": the dialer picks the least busy pool number per call (default, included with any plan). "dedicated": pin one number this organization has claimed. |
| `caller_id.phone_number_id` | string (uuid) |  | Required for "dedicated", forbidden for "shared_pool". Get ids from list_caller_ids. |
| `outcome_fields` | array of object {key, label, type, options, is_kpi} |  | What to extract from each conversation. Declare these BEFORE calls run: without them results only contain a free-text summary, no structured answers. A field the caller never answered comes back null. |
| `outcome_fields[].key` | string | yes | Machine key, e.g. "paid" or "callback_date". |
| `outcome_fields[].label` | string | yes | Human label, e.g. "Paid?". |
| `outcome_fields[].type` | `"text"` \| `"number"` \| `"boolean"` \| `"enum"` \| `"json"` | yes |  |
| `outcome_fields[].options` | array of string |  | Allowed values; only for type "enum". |
| `outcome_fields[].is_kpi` | boolean |  | Highlight as a headline KPI on the campaign overview. |
| `scheduled_start_at` | string (date-time) |  | Call at this time instead of straight away (ISO 8601). |
| `max_attempts` | integer (min 1, max 10) |  | Total tries if nobody picks up (default 1: one call, no redials). |
| `wait_seconds` | integer (min 0, max 80) |  | Wait up to this long for the call to finish and return its result. Default 0 (return immediately). Max 80; time spent waiting for the content review counts toward that 80 s ceiling. |

### `get_call_result`

`read-only`

The state and outcome of a call placed with make_call (or the latest calls of any campaign): whether it is finished, how it ended (completed, declined, no_answer, busy, failed, voicemail), duration, summary, key points, extracted answers, sentiment and the full transcript. Poll every ~5 s until finished is true.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaign_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Campaign id (for make_call, the campaign_id it returned). |

### `list_campaign_calls`

`read-only`

Lists call attempts in a campaign, newest last by default, with status, outcome, duration and extracted data. Use get_call for a transcript. Status runs queued → dialing → ringing → answered → completed, with declined, no_answer, busy and failed as other endings.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaign_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Campaign id (for make_call, the campaign_id it returned). |
| `page` | integer (min 1, max 9007199254740991) |  | 1-based page number. Default 1. |
| `take` | integer (min 1, max 50) |  | Items per page, 1–50. Default 10. |
| `order` | `"ASC"` \| `"DESC"` |  |  |

### `get_call`

`read-only`

One call in full: outcome, sentiment, summary, key points, action items, extracted answers, latency metrics, cost, and the turn-by-turn transcript.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaign_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Campaign id (for make_call, the campaign_id it returned). |
| `call_id` | string | yes | The call id, e.g. "CALL-20260920-a1b2c3d4e5f60718" (from list_campaign_calls or get_call_result). Not a UUID. |

### `get_call_recording_url`

`read-only`

A short-lived signed URL to the audio recording of a call. Expires quickly, so hand it to the user promptly. It is a link only; the audio itself is not returned.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campaign_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Campaign id (for make_call, the campaign_id it returned). |
| `call_id` | string | yes | The call id, e.g. "CALL-20260920-a1b2c3d4e5f60718". |

## Analytics

### `get_analytics_overview`

`read-only`

Headline numbers for the whole organization over a period: calls, answer rate, talk time, spend, each with its change against the previous period, plus a twelve-month trend. Default period: month.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `period` | `"day"` \| `"week"` \| `"month"` \| `"quarter"` \| `"year"` |  | Window to report on. Compared against the equal-length window before it. |

### `get_analytics_report`

`read-only`

Detailed report over a period: call volume over time, how calls ended (shares that add up), average call time, no-answer rate and answer rate. Default period: week.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `period` | `"day"` \| `"week"` \| `"month"` \| `"quarter"` \| `"year"` |  | Window to report on. Compared against the equal-length window before it. |

## undefined

### `list_support_tickets`

`read-only`

Lists the organization's CXCaller support tickets, most recently active first, each with its reference (e.g. CX-1001), subject, status and last message. Status: open (waiting for support), in_progress (support is on it), waiting_on_you (support replied and needs an answer), resolved. hasUnreadUpdate is true when support has the last word.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | integer (min 1, max 9007199254740991) |  | 1-based page number. Default 1. |
| `take` | integer (min 1, max 50) |  | Items per page, 1–50. Default 10. |
| `query` | string |  | Search by reference or subject. |
| `status` | array of `"open"` \| `"in_progress"` \| `"waiting_on_you"` \| `"resolved"` |  | Only tickets in these statuses. |

### `get_support_ticket`

`read-only`

One support ticket with its full conversation (messages from the organization and from CXCaller support) and status history.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ticket_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Ticket id (not the "CX-1001" reference). |

### `create_support_ticket`

`changes data`

Opens a ticket with CXCaller support, which is emailed about it. Use it for problems the user wants CXCaller staff to look at (failing calls, billing, numbers, account). It is written under this API key's name and is visible to everyone in the organization's Help Center. Include ids (campaign, call) and what was expected vs. what happened. Limited to 10 per hour per organization.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `subject` | string | yes |  |
| `category` | `"campaigns"` \| `"phone_numbers"` \| `"contacts"` \| `"billing"` \| `"account"` \| `"other"` | yes |  |
| `priority` | `"low"` \| `"normal"` \| `"high"` \| `"urgent"` |  | Default normal. |
| `description` | string | yes | The first message: the problem in full. |

### `reply_to_support_ticket`

`changes data`

Adds a message to a ticket, written under this API key's name. Replying to a resolved or waiting_on_you ticket reopens it (status open).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ticket_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Ticket id (not the "CX-1001" reference). |
| `body` | string | yes |  |

### `set_support_ticket_status`

`changes data`

Marks a ticket resolved, or reopens it. Only CXCaller support can set the other statuses.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ticket_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Ticket id (not the "CX-1001" reference). |
| `status` | `"open"` \| `"resolved"` | yes |  |

### `get_support_attachment_url`

`read-only`

A short-lived download URL for a file attached to a ticket message (ids from get_support_ticket). It expires at expiresAt.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ticket_id` | string (uuid) | yes | Ticket id (not the "CX-1001" reference). |
| `attachment_id` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

### `get_support_chat`

`read-only`

The organization's live chat with CXCaller support (one thread per organization), oldest first. Without `after`: the latest 200 messages. To wait for an answer, poll every 10 s or so with `after` set to the newest createdAt you have; it returns only newer messages. Author is user, support, or automated (the canned acknowledgement).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `after` | string (date-time) |  | Only messages strictly after this ISO 8601 instant. |

### `send_support_chat_message`

`changes data`

Sends a message to CXCaller support's live chat, written under this API key's name. The first message after 24 h of silence also gets an automated acknowledgement, returned alongside it. Staff answer when they are online; read replies with get_support_chat. For anything that needs tracking, prefer create_support_ticket.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `body` | string | yes |  |
